idiom_name: hand-written link-table mapper over the sqlite3 C API (composite key + two foreign keys)
implementation_notes: C has no mapping layer at all, so the pattern is entirely hand-written: a CREATE TABLE with two foreign keys and PRIMARY KEY (a_id, b_id), plus insert, delete and read functions around the sqlite3 C API. The composite key is what replaces the mapper class an object language would write - it is the only thing preventing duplicate links, since no object in the program holds the association. Declare ON DELETE CASCADE on both foreign keys so removing an end removes its links, and remember that SQLite enforces foreign keys only after PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON on every connection. Buffered or batched reads (one prepared statement, one pass over the result set) are what keep a collection load from becoming one query per row.
pitfalls: PRAGMA foreign_keys is off by default and is set per connection: a helper that opens its own connection writes orphan links unless it enables the pragma too.

There is no change tracking: after an object is loaded, edits to its collection must be diffed and turned into explicit INSERT/DELETE calls, and composite-key rows cannot be UPDATEd - unlink and relink.
A collection read that prepares a statement per element turns a join into N+1; prepare once and bind the owner key.

Skipping ON DELETE CASCADE or explicit link cleanup lets endpoint deletion leave orphan rows; declare the cascade and enable SQLite foreign keys on every connection, or delete links in the same transaction.
